study_identification_part.si4_title: Accommodating Site Variation In Neuroimaging Data Using Normative And Hierarchical Bayesian Models

cm1_research_objectives.reason: The abstract states the purpose of accommodating site effects in normative modeling via hierarchical Bayesian models, compares linear and non-linear versions, and notes the clinical autism application to test retention of clinically useful information.
cm1_research_objectives.supporting_text: "In this study, we suggest accommodating for these site effects by including them as random effects in a hierarchical Bayesian model. We compared the performance of a linear and a non-linear hierarchical Bayesian model in modeling the effect of age on cortical thickness... In addition, we used data from individuals with autism to test whether our models are able to retain clinically useful information while removing site effects."

nm1_selection_criteria_reference_cohort.reason: The study identifies the reference cohort as ABIDE controls (n=569) and reports sex counts and that cortical thickness outliers were removed, but does not provide detailed inclusion/exclusion criteria or reasons for participant exclusion beyond outlier removal.
nm1_selection_criteria_reference_cohort.supporting_text: "The consortium provides a publicly available... data set... For this study, we used 569 controls for development and performance testing of the models, out of which 470 were male." / "Measures of cortical thickness were extracted... scanned for outliers... criterion... above or beyond 2 inter quartile ranges... This leads to the removal of 1055 out of 162905 data points (0.006%)."

nm2_handling_of_covariates_reference_coh.reason: Age and sex are used as covariates in the models, and site is included as a random effect in the hierarchical Bayesian models with comparisons that preserve age and sex effects.
nm2_handling_of_covariates_reference_coh.supporting_text: "We developed and compared two versions of a hierarchical Bayesian models that include site as a predictor... Hierarchical Bayesian Linear Model... Gaussian Process for age... Both hierarchical Bayesian models were trained and tested in a within-site split." / "site effects are first harmonized... then a simple Bayesian linear algorithm, with an additive term for age and sex, but without site as a predictor is used to make predictions in Stan."

nm3_data_sources_reference_cohort.reason: The reference cohort is explicitly described as the publicly available ABIDE dataset with citation and link.
nm3_data_sources_reference_cohort.supporting_text: "The consortium provides a publicly available structural magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) data set... For this study, we used 569 controls... The data were processed... as part of the Preprocessed Connectomes Project... download on the preprocessed section of the ABIDE initiative."

nm4_image_acquisition_protocol.reason: Imaging data were obtained from the existing multi-site ABIDE dataset rather than collected primarily in this study, so primary acquisition parameters are out of scope.
nm4_image_acquisition_protocol.supporting_text: "The ABIDE consortium... provides a publicly available... MRI data set... aggregated data from 20 independent samples collected at 17 different scanning locations."

nm5_data_preprocessing.reason: They describe preprocessing via the standardized FreeSurfer pipeline from the Preprocessed Connectomes Project, outlier detection on cortical thickness values, and hemisphere averaging.
nm5_data_preprocessing.supporting_text: "The data were processed using a standardized protocol (Craddock et al., 2013) of the FreeSurfer standard pipeline... Measures of cortical thickness were extracted... scanned for outliers... criterion... above or beyond 2 inter quartile ranges... values of right and left hemisphere... were averaged."

nm6_internal_data_validation_reference_c.reason: The healthy control data were split into training (70%, n=389) and test (30%, n=166) sets while preserving age, sex, and site distribution, providing a held-out partition for validation.
nm6_internal_data_validation_reference_c.supporting_text: "we split the the healthy control data set into a training set (70% of data, n=389) and a test set (30% of data, n=166)... distribution of age, sex and site was preserved between sets. Thus, training and test sets contained individuals from the same sites ('withinsite-split')."

nm7_external_data_validation_reference_c.reason: Model evaluation used only internal ABIDE control splits; no independent external healthy dataset was applied for validation.
nm7_external_data_validation_reference_c.supporting_text: "training set (70%... n=389) and a test set (30%... n=166)... training and test sets contained individuals from the same sites ('withinsite-split')."

nm8_normative_modeling_approach.reason: They detail hierarchical Bayesian linear and Gaussian process models with site random effects, describe comparison harmonization models, and specify implementation in Stan.
nm8_normative_modeling_approach.supporting_text: "two versions of a hierarchical Bayesian models that include site as a predictor... random effect for site... Gaussian Process for age... ('HBLM', 'HBGPM')." / "site effects are first harmonized... and then a simple Bayesian linear algorithm... is used to make predictions in Stan... Predictions made from raw data... were used as a baseline model."

nm9_model_performance_reference_cohort.reason: Performance metrics (correlation, SRMSE, log-likelihood, explained variance, MSLL) are described and results comparing models are reported.
nm9_model_performance_reference_cohort.supporting_text: "Model performance is assessed using... Pearson's correlation coefficient... standardized... root mean squared error (SRMSE)... log-likelihood... proportion of variance explained (EV)... mean standardized log-loss (MSLL)." / "HBLM and the HBGPM showed higher... rho... lower... SRMSEs... smaller... LL and higher... EV than all comparison models."

cr1_selection_criteria_clinical_cohort.supporting_text: "we applied the hierarchical Bayesian models to 482 individuals with autism from the same data set, out of which 430 were male." / "Measures of cortical thickness were... scanned for outliers... criterion... above or beyond 2 inter quartile ranges... removal of 1055 out of 162905 data points."

cr6_interpretation_of_deviation_scores.supporting_text: "We define a z-score of +/- 1.96 based on the training set as atypical value, thus marking an individual that lies above or below the 95% percentile... average percentage of individuals with extreme z-scores is 5.7%... controls...
